lifeForceRecovery.maximumCap: LifeForce cannot be restored above its calculated maximum
lifeForceRecovery.roundingForFractionalRestoration: round up to the next whole LifeForce point
lifeForceRecovery.restDurations: Light rest 4 hours; full rest 8 hours
lifeForceRecovery.woundInteraction: LifeForce regeneration does not remove Wounds; full rest separately recovers 1 Wound

manaRecovery.roundingForFractionalRestoration: round up to the next whole Mana point
manaRecovery.maximumCap: Mana cannot be restored above its maximum

restRule.lightRest: Restore 50% of maximum LifeForce and Mana (round up to whole points), capped at maximum
restRule.fullRest: Restore both LifeForce and Mana to full maximum and recover 1 Wound (minimum remaining Wounds 0)
restRule.wounds: A full 8-hour rest recovers 1 Wound; a 4-hour light rest restores no Wounds

combat.physicalDefense: Attack-type-dependent: melee uses Parry + applicable Block; ranged uses Dodge + applicable Block. Dodge does not defend melee; Parry does not defend ranged.
combat.avoidableSpellDefense: Magical projectile: Dodge + Spell Resistance (+ Block only from magic-blocking shield); melee spell: Parry + Spell Resistance (+ Block only from magic-blocking shield)
combat.damagePerSuccess: Damage from damaging weapons and abilities scales directly with the number of attack successes; each weapon or ability defines its own damage per success.

resistanceCalculation.damageTypeHandling: apply only to matching damage type; mixed-type hits have their portions calculated separately
resistanceCalculation.notes: At 5% resistance, 1 incoming matching damage is fully prevented; balance impact on small attacks should be playtested.

mixedDamageResistance.rule: For attacks with multiple damage types, divide incoming damage by damage type and resolve applicable resistance on each component separately, using the approved floor with minimum 1 prevention for positive matching resistance and damage.
mixedDamageResistance.perTypeFormula: min(componentDamage, max(1, floor(componentDamage * applicableResistancePercent / 100))) when both componentDamage and applicableResistancePercent are positive; otherwise zero
mixedDamageResistance.order: After per-type resistance, magical shield pools absorb eligible damage types (all by default unless ability restrictions); remaining type-specific components pass to armor only where armor protects those types, then to LifeForce and Wounds.
mixedDamageResistance.shieldArmorHandling: How subsequent shield and armor mitigation is allocated among remaining damage types is pending.

equipment.mechanic: Grants Block percentage to reduce attackers' chance to hit
equipment.canBlockMagicIf: Shield has an explicit magic-blocking item property

magical.mechanic: Grants magical shield mitigation pool that absorbs damage after resistance and before armor

armorMitigation.magicalArmorException: Some magical armor restores its mitigation pool over time as specified by the armor's own properties
armorMitigation.poolSize: Each armor item has its own Rank 0 base mitigation, set when that armor type is created. Maximum item mitigation at an equipment Rank is ceil(item base mitigation × approved Rank multiplier), subject to the Light/Medium/Heavy category maximum at that Rank.

fieldRepairs.skillRequirement: appropriate Crafting skill for armor material and type
fieldRepairs.capInterpretation: Field repairs may be repeated, but armor's current mitigation pool cannot be raised above 25% of its original maximum mitigation pool by field repairs
fieldRepairs.availability: Only if armor durability is greater than zero

fullRepairs.zeroDurabilityRepair: workshop required before field repairs become available again

durability.description: Armor has Durability points analogous to wounds; each event in which its mitigation pool is depleted to zero costs one Durability point.
durability.onPoolDepleted: Lose 1 Durability when the mitigation pool transitions from positive to zero; further damage at zero does not deduct additional Durability until it has been restored and depleted again
durability.atZero: No field repairs possible until repaired at an appropriate workshop
durability.maximumDurability: Fixed whole-number value set when each armor type is designed; does not change with equipment Rank.
durability.maximumDurabilityStatus: Approved: armor-type-specific fixed maximum durability, independent of equipment Rank. Numeric values pending item design.

rankScaling.status: superseded: durability does not scale by Rank
rankScaling.rule: Each armor type has a fixed maximum durability assigned during item design; armor of any Rank retains that armor type's durability value.
rankScaling.rounding: Not applicable; durability is specified directly as a whole number

ordinaryArmor.doesNotAbsorb: All non-Physical damage types unless explicitly given protection by a special property

magicalArmor.additionalDamageTypes: Only damage types explicitly specified by the individual magical armor's properties

damageTypeProtection.mixedDamageHandling: Keep type-specific components distinct through armor mitigation. Apply armor's mitigation pool only to components whose damage type that armor protects against; other components bypass armor and proceed to LifeForce/Wounds.
damageTypeProtection.magicalShieldDamageTypeHandling: Ability-created magical shield pools absorb all damage types by default, unless the ability specifies restricted coverage; allocation for mixed attacks when pool is insufficient remains pending.

equipmentRanks.rankNames: Same names and rank scale as character ranks
equipmentRanks.equipRestriction: A character cannot equip or use an item whose rank exceeds their character rank

maximumMitigationByCategoryAndRank.status: Approved maximum mitigation for ranks 0 through 3; ranks 4 through 10 pending
maximumMitigationByCategoryAndRank.rule: Category-by-rank values are upper caps for individually designed armor types, not automatic identical mitigation values for all armor in that category.
maximumMitigationByCategoryAndRank.capTable: Ranks 0-3 approved in approvedMaximums; ranks 4-10 pending
maximumMitigationByCategoryAndRank.rounding: Round up to the nearest whole mitigation point using ceiling
maximumMitigationByCategoryAndRank.rankThreeMilestone: Amethyst is the first major soul-strengthening power threshold and Soul Weapon manifestation

itemBaseMitigation.assignedWhen: When an individual armor type is designed/created
itemBaseMitigation.value: A nonnegative whole-point base mitigation specific to that armor type; not automatically identical for every armor in its category
itemBaseMitigation.categoryLimit: At Rank 0 the armor item's base cannot exceed its category maximum: Light 5, Medium 10, Heavy 15
itemBaseMitigation.rankMultipliers: Ranks 0–3 use approved multipliers 1, 1.5, 2, 3; later ranks deferred
itemBaseMitigation.maximum: Cannot exceed the category maximum mitigation at that equipment Rank
itemBaseMitigation.example: Rank 0 Heavy armor with individual base mitigation 12 has Rank 1 mitigation ceil(12×1.5)=18; the category cap is 23.

physicalDefenseByAttackType.notes: Block may apply to either melee or ranged when the defender has applicable Block. The interaction of these values with attack rolls and their exact calculations remain pending.

combat.spellDefenseInteractionStatus: Attack categories and default magic-block restriction approved; detailed calculations pending

magicalProjectile.conditionalDefense: Block only if equipped shield explicitly has property allowing magical attacks to be blocked

meleeSpellAttack.conditionalDefense: Block only if equipped shield explicitly has property allowing magical attacks to be blocked

spellDefense.note: Special shield properties can enable Block against magic, but ordinary equipment shields cannot. Exact accuracy and defense resolution remain pending.

attackVsDefense.hitCondition: On attack d100: natural 96-100 always misses; otherwise natural 01-05 always hits; otherwise hit only if roll <= final attack target.
attackVsDefense.successes: Normal hit: 1 + floor((final attack target - roll)/10). For automatic hits when roll exceeds final target and final target <= 5, assign 1 normal success.
attackVsDefense.applicableDefense: Use melee/ranged and magic-defense restrictions already established
attackVsDefense.minimumAndMaximumTargets: The raw final target may be zero or negative; natural 01-05 always hits. Upper target cap remains pending.
attackVsDefense.criticalInteraction: When final attack target is 5 or less, natural 01-05 is an automatic normal hit with 1 success and no +3 critical successes. When final attack target is greater than 5, a natural 01-05 hit gains the existing +3 critical successes.
attackVsDefense.notes: Defense subtraction modifies both chance to hit and number of successes; account for applicable situational attack modifiers as part of modified attack skill

attackRollEdgeCases.scope: Attack rolls; general non-attack skill critical rules unchanged
attackRollEdgeCases.automaticMissPenalty: Ordinary miss; no additional critical-failure penalty by default

damageScaling.damagePerSuccessSource: Defined individually by the weapon or ability
damageScaling.application: On successful damaging attacks or abilities, including bonus successes from critical rolls
damageScaling.specialModifiers: Apply explicitly defined additional damage and typed effects per their individual rules; interaction/order pending item and ability design
damageScaling.values: Weapon and ability damage-per-success values pending equipment and ability design
damageScaling.example: 3 damage per success with 4 successes deals 12 damage before resistances and mitigation

magicalShieldMitigation.defaultDamageTypeCoverage: All incoming damage types, including Physical and elemental damage
magicalShieldMitigation.exceptions: Individual abilities may explicitly limit shield coverage to specified damage types
magicalShieldMitigation.damageOrder: After applicable damage resistance and before armor mitigation
magicalShieldMitigation.poolBehavior: Absorbs eligible incoming damage up to remaining magical shield mitigation pool capacity
magicalShieldMitigation.allocationAcrossMixedDamage: Approved: allocate eligible Physical damage first. For two or more eligible non-Physical damage types, attacker chooses their order when declaring the attack, before defender resistance and mitigation are resolved. Then allocate the remaining shield pool in that declared order.

allocationExample.note: Example assumes shield protects both types; leftover Fire bypasses ordinary armor.

nonPhysicalDamagePriority.declaredWhen: attack is declared, before defender resistances and mitigation calculations
nonPhysicalDamagePriority.appliesTo: multiple eligible non-Physical damage types in a mixed-damage attack
nonPhysicalDamagePriority.physicalPriority: Physical always precedes non-Physical damage regardless of attacker preference

stacking.comparison: Compare the current shield's remaining mitigation points against the newly offered shield's mitigation points (not the old shield's original maximum).
stacking.replacementChoice: The shield's recipient/target may choose to keep the existing shield or accept the new shield regardless of which has more mitigation points.
stacking.onAcceptNew: New shield replaces the old shield entirely; use new shield's full offered pool, coverage, and other properties. Pools never combine.
stacking.onKeepOld: Newly offered shield does not replace the old one; retain existing pool, coverage, and properties.
stacking.strongerShieldRule: A stronger newly offered shield does not automatically replace the existing shield; target chooses.
stacking.weakerOrEqualShieldRule: The target may accept a weaker or equal-pool new shield to gain more useful damage-type coverage or other properties.
stacking.scope: Ability-created magical shield mitigation pools; equipment Block shields remain separate
stacking.example: Fire shield with 22 remaining versus new Arcane Barrier with 20 offered: target may accept Arcane Barrier to gain all-type protection or keep Fire shield.

sameShieldRecast.rule: Recasting an active shield generates a new pool. The target may accept it to replace the existing shield or keep the existing shield. Pools do not add together.
sameShieldRecast.example: An 8/20 barrier recast for 20 becomes 20/20 if accepted.

duration.duration: Determined individually by the ability creating the magical shield
endConditions: The remaining shield mitigation pool reaches zero
duration.rule: The magical shield ends immediately when either condition occurs
duration.recasting: An accepted replacement shield uses the new casting's duration and mitigation, rather than extending the old shield

maintenance.defaultBehavior: Once cast, an ability-created magical shield persists independently without concentration or ongoing Mana expenditure until its ability-specific duration expires or its mitigation pool reaches zero.
maintenance.exceptions: An individual shield ability may explicitly require concentration, recurring Mana, or other upkeep.
maintenance.initialCastingCost: Set by individual ability; not altered by this rule

dispelling.requirement: A dispelling magical effect must be sufficiently powerful to overcome the active magical shield
dispelling.onSuccess: The active magical shield ends immediately, removing its remaining mitigation and protection
dispelling.exactMechanics: Dispel contest, strength comparison, targeting, and success conditions pending magic ability design
dispelling.notes: Dispelling is an alternative to depleting the mitigation pool or waiting for duration expiry

statusTab.currentMitigation: Nonnegative whole-number pool; 0 means no active shield
statusTab.remainingDuration: Determined by the ability creating the shield; editable text to support ability-specific duration units until power and effect automation
statusTab.depletion: Shield ends immediately when mitigation reaches 0; clear remaining duration
statusTab.expiration: Shield ends when ability duration expires, even if mitigation remains; manual removal for now
statusTab.reapplication: A newly applied magical shield replaces or is rejected according to existing one-active-shield rules; no stacking or automatic recharge

areaOfEffectDefense.shieldPools: Each target uses only their own active magical shield mitigation pool; no shared mitigation across targets
areaOfEffectDefense.damageTypeRules: Apply established damage type resistance, magical shield priority, and armor coverage separately for each target
areaOfEffectDefense.attackAndSaveMechanics: One attack roll against all affected targets is approved; any saving-throw alternatives or ability-specific exceptions remain to be defined.

attackRoll.rule: Make one d100 attack roll for the AoE ability and compare that same roll separately with each affected target's final attack target after subtracting their applicable defenses.
attackRoll.perTargetTargetFormula: modified ability accuracy percentage - sum(target's applicable defense percentages)
attackRoll.perTargetHit: Apply approved natural 01-05 automatic hit and natural 96-100 automatic miss rules, otherwise roll <= target's final attack target
attackRoll.successes: Each successfully hit target computes its own number of successes from its own final attack target and the shared roll, including existing critical roll handling.
attackRoll.damageAndMitigation: Resolve damage, resistances, shield, armor, LifeForce and Wounds independently per target
attackRoll.exceptions: Ability-specific unavoidable effects and other expressly different targeting mechanics to be specified during ability design

damageScaling.attackRoll: One shared d100 roll per area-of-effect attack
damageScaling.perTargetSuccesses: Calculate success count separately for each affected target, based on the shared roll and that target's final hit target after applicable defense
damageScaling.perTargetDamageFormula: If the attack hits target: targetDamage = targetSuccesses * abilityDamagePerSuccess; otherwise 0
damageScaling.criticalRolls: Existing natural 01-05 critical/automatic-hit rules apply individually based on each target's final attack target
damageScaling.perTargetMitigation: Resolve each target's resistance, active magical shield, applicable armor, LifeForce, and Wounds independently
damageScaling.exceptions: Abilities with expressly different effects are specified during ability design

friendlyFire.defaultRule: Area-of-effect attacks affect all valid creatures inside the affected area, including allies, enemies, and the caster if inside the area.
friendlyFire.exceptions: An individual ability may explicitly exclude allies, the caster, or designated creatures.
friendlyFire.targetResolution: Apply the established single shared d100 attack roll separately against each affected creature's defenses, with per-target successes, damage and mitigation.
friendlyFire.targetingAndGeometry: Exact area dimensions, targeting rules and placement restrictions pending ability design.

cover.rule: A target receives cover-based defensive protection against an area-effect attack when cover genuinely protects that target and lies between the target and the effect's point of origin.
cover.direction: Assess cover relative to the AoE effect's origin rather than simply the caster's position.
cover.noProtection: Cover not interposed between the effect origin and target provides no cover bonus against that effect.
cover.effectSpecificExceptions: Effects that bypass, originate within, or otherwise circumvent cover may negate it according to their ability rules.
cover.specificCoverBonuses: Partial cover +10 percentage points defense; heavy cover +20 percentage points; full cover prevents direct targeting through obstruction unless bypassed, penetrated, or destroyed.

partial.rule: Add 10 percentage points to applicable defense against an attack when cover protects the target

heavy.rule: Add 20 percentage points to applicable defense against an attack when cover protects the target

full.rule: Cannot be directly targeted through the obstruction; an attack that penetrates or destroys the obstruction or otherwise bypasses it may affect the target

cover.application: Physical attacks and applicable magical attacks, including AoE where cover lies between the target and effect origin
cover.calculation: Cover is an applicable defense bonus deducted from the attacker's modified attack target
cover.geometryAndDurability: Exact criteria for classifying partial versus heavy cover, object durability, penetration, and destruction pending

destructibleCover.rule: Destructible cover objects have their own mitigation pool and durability score, separate from creatures' armor and shields.
destructibleCover.interaction: Attacks that can damage an obstruction may deplete its mitigation and affect its durability; exact breakage/penetration rules pending objects and terrain design.
destructibleCover.values: Set by material, construction and object type during objects/terrain design; no numerical defaults approved yet.

foundrySheet.fields: To be designed; anticipated mitigation and durability at minimum

damageCarryThrough.rule: When an attack destroys intervening cover and is capable of penetrating that obstruction, unabsorbed damage continues through toward a creature behind the cover.
damageCarryThrough.calculation: Remaining damage after resolving damage absorbed by the cover carries through to the target; then apply target-specific applicable defenses/mitigation as relevant under rules still to be defined.
damageCarryThrough.nonPenetrating: If attack cannot penetrate the cover, it cannot deal carry-through damage to the creature behind it.
damageCarryThrough.detailedResolution: How attack accuracy, cover mitigation, durability, and target hit resolution work during penetration deferred until objects/terrain design.
damageCarryThrough.example: An attack deals 20 damage and a penetrable barricade absorbs 12 before destruction; remaining 8 may reach a creature behind it.

initiative.system: Action Score (adapted from user's HWFWM game)
initiative.prowessInterpretation: Use the tens digit of the percentage Prowess score (integer tens, e.g. Prowess 37 gives +3)
initiative.priority: The combatant with the highest current remaining Action Score acts next; recalculate priority after actions spend score
initiative.actionSpending: Every non-free action category (movement, basic attacks, abilities, etc.) has an Action Score cost deducted when performed
initiative.affordability: Specific minimum cost, free actions and handling of unaffordable actions pending detailed action economy
initiative.roundEnd: The round ends once no combatant has Action Score available to take a permitted paid action; precise stop/pass rules pending
initiative.actionCosts: Deferred at user's request until returning to action economy; movement remains 2 Action Score as approved; basic attacks and other costs not approved

tieBreaking.first: Highest current remaining Action Score acts first
tieBreaking.second: If current Action Scores tie, higher full Prowess percentage acts first
tieBreaking.third: If full Prowess values also tie, roll d20 for each tied combatant; highest roll acts first
tieBreaking.rerolls: Reroll tied d20 roll-offs until resolved
tieBreaking.timing: Determine order whenever combatants tie for highest available Action Score

initiative.newRoundGeneration: Approved: new round Action Score = prior round remaining Action Score (positive, zero, or negative) + 1d20 + floor(Prowess / 10) + applicable modifiers
initiative.notes: Replaces prior proposed Prowess roll-under initiative by successes; initiative is current Action Score, not a separate initiative check.

carryover.negativeExample: Previous balance -6; roll 11; Prowess 47 yields +4; no other modifiers: new score = -6+11+4 = 9
carryover.notes: Overspending and precise round end timing still require separate approval; do not infer that negative carryover itself allows voluntary overspending.

overspending.rule: If remaining Action Score is positive, a combatant may perform a paid action even when its cost is greater than remaining score, potentially making the balance negative.
overspending.afterAction: At zero or negative score, no further normal paid actions that round.
overspending.carryover: Negative balances carry forward to the next round.

movementAction.distance: Up to the character's full movement pace for one movement action
movementAction.costModel: Flat 2 Action Score per movement action for any positive distance up to full movement pace, not a per-space cost.
movementAction.partialMovementCost: Approved: flat 2 Action Score for moving any positive distance up to the character's full movement pace; no reduction for fewer spaces.
movementAction.multipleMovementActions: Approved: characters may take multiple movement actions in the same round; each costs 2 Action Score and moves any positive distance up to full pace.
movementAction.movementModes: Use applicable character movement speed; detailed terrain/flight/swimming costs pending
movementAction.notes: The player rejected per-space costs in favor of 2 Action Score to move full pace.
movementAction.turnOrder: After each movement action, subtract 2 Action Score and recalculate who has the highest remaining score before the next action.
movementAction.actionEligibility: Uses established Action Score rules, including a final action that can take positive remaining score negative.

dodge.cannotEvade: Dodge becomes 0 while unconscious, immobilized, dead, or otherwise physically unable to evade.
dodge.attackInteraction: Subtract applicable Dodge percentage from modified attack accuracy; affects hit target and success count.
dodge.specialBonuses: Equipment, talent and ability modifiers deferred.

parry.formula: floor(Might / 10) + equipped melee weapon Parry rating
parry.weaponContribution: Each melee weapon has a Parry rating, defined when equipment is designed.
parry.applicability: Melee attacks, including melee spell attacks under existing spell-defense rules; no Parry against ranged attacks.
parry.accuracyEffect: Subtract Parry from attacker's modified accuracy when applicable; impacts hit chance and successes.
parry.sheetInterim: Until equipment items are implemented, an editable equipped-melee-weapon Parry rating models its contribution.
parry.unarmedOrNoWeapon: No weapon contribution unless an applicable equipment/rule grants one; equipment rules pending
parry.incapacitationInteraction: Same as Dodge: effective Parry is 0 when unconscious, immobilized, dead, or otherwise physically unable to defend. Base Parry and weapon rating remain tracked.
parry.multipleWeapons: How to select/combine ratings pending equipment rules.
parry.effectiveParry: If incapacitated (same flag/conditions as Dodge), 0; otherwise floor(Might / 10) + equipped melee weapon Parry rating.

block.enduranceContribution: floor(floor(Endurance / 10) / 2); always whole percentage points, rounded down
block.noEquippedShield: Block 0; Endurance contribution applies only when a shield is equipped
block.applicability: Equipment shields can Block melee and ranged physical attacks
block.magic: Equipment shield cannot Block magic unless its item has an explicit magic-blocking property
block.attackInteraction: Block subtracts from attack accuracy and can reduce successes per existing defense system
block.incapacitation: Same as Dodge and Parry: effective Block 0 when unconscious, immobilized, dead, or otherwise unable to physically defend; shield rating remains unchanged.
block.sheetInterim: Toggle equipped shield and enter its Block rating manually until equipment Items are implemented

spellResistance.application: Subtract against spell attacks as determined by existing spell-defense categories, including magical projectiles, melee spell attacks, and unavoidable spells
spellResistance.interactionWithOtherDefenses: Stack applicable Dodge or Parry where the attack type permits; equipment Block applies to magic only with explicit magic-blocking property
spellResistance.incapacitation: Spell Resistance remains fully active when unconscious, immobilized, dead, or otherwise physically unable to defend. It is inherent rather than dependent on movement.
spellResistance.cost: passive, no action or resource cost established
spellResistance.effectiveFormula: floor(Intellect / 10), including while incapacitated; independent of Dodge/Parry/Block suppression

recovery.higherRankHealingAbilities: May restore Wounds; exact abilities and quantities pending

bleedingToDeath.enduranceSave: d100 roll-under current Endurance minus 5 percentage points per prior failed death save
bleedingToDeath.saveFrequency: each turn while Bleeding to Death; exact turn timing in Foundry combat automation pending
bleedingToDeath.success: One successful save stabilizes the character
bleedingToDeath.failure: Each failure increases failures by one and imposes -5 percentage points to the next save TN
bleedingToDeath.death: Third failed save results in death
bleedingToDeath.criticalAutoSuccess: Natural 01–05 always succeeds per standard roll convention

soulWeapon.identity: unique physical manifestation of the wielder's soul
soulWeapon.progression: grows with wielder; mechanical details pending

futureMarks.eldritchFormation: standardized combination of Power, Specialization, Elemental, and Concept Marks; enhances Soul Weapon and familiar; neither determines Eldritch identity

magicCosmology.originPrinciple: Magic originates in the Astral in its pure form

markOfPurposeGrantedAbilities.delivery: Automatically granted by the chosen Mark of Purpose
markOfPurposeGrantedAbilities.abilityDefinitions: Specific active and passive effects pending individual Mark design, starting with Defender
markOfPurposeGrantedAbilities.additionalLearnedAbilities: Separate ability creation and acquisition rules pending
markOfPurposeGrantedAbilities.activeCosts: Defined when individual abilities are designed; activated powers use Mana under the existing resources rule
